title: Plant species in nested plots
body: A team of ecology students surveyed flowering plant species in nested plots of increasing area within one forested region of the Western Ghats. When they plotted species richness (S) against area (A) on ordinary axes, the points formed a curve that rose steeply at first and then levelled off, like a rectangular hyperbola. When they plotted log S against log A, the points fell on a straight line described by log S = log C + Z log A, where C is the Y-intercept. The slope of their line, Z, was 0.2, which lies within the range of 0.1 to 0.2 reported for many taxa within a region. They then compared their result with published data for frugivorous birds and mammals in tropical forests of different continents, where the slope is about 1.15.
